usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice
Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is pretrained Qwen3-4B loaded from the local asset snapshot with dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation='sdpa', local_files_only=True, in eval mode on context['device'].
Numerical policy matches common.configure(): torch.manual_seed(20261020), matmul/cudnn TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark disabled, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', 4 CPU threads, 1 interop thread.
Input is real data: the chat-templated source prompt encoded without special tokens, tiled and truncated to exactly 256 prompt tokens, replicated across batch=1, resident on GPU.
Decoding is greedy argmax over the last-position logits; no sampling, temperature, EOS stopping, or early exit; exactly 32 tokens are generated.
Every forward uses use_cache=True with a KV cache created fresh per run; decode steps feed exactly one token; logits_to_keep=1 as in the source.
ttft boundary is the source's explicit torch.cuda.synchronize() immediately after the first forward/argmax; the workload boundary is the final torch.cuda.synchronize() after the last decode step.
The full workload (prefill plus all 31 decode steps) always executes, in every mode, even though the objective measures only the first-token phase.
Quality comparison uses the source tolerances (atol=rtol=0.02 on logits) and exact greedy token equality; no accuracy or convergence beyond reference fidelity is claimed.
No CUDA initialization or model loading at import time; no second reference model is allocated on GPU; the process group (none here, single process) is never destroyed.

selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose boundary is the prefill forward on the 256-token prompt plus argmax and the explicit first-token synchronize; decode work (374.7 ms diagnostic CUDA vs 21.5 ms for prefill) is outside the metric, so only prefill-phase groups can move the project objective. Inside that boundary the dominant leaf is group 0c566a3a363f294c6750: the 72 gate_proj/up_proj GEMMs (aten.linear.default, single signature [1,256,2560] x [9728,2560] bf16, one per projection per layer across all 36 layers), 7656 us diagnostic CUDA = 47% of all prefill aten::linear time (16377 us) and ~36% of the 21.5 ms prefill CUDA total. Each call is one M=256, N=9728, K=2560 TN bf16 GEMM taking 103-108 us in ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_bf16_64x128_sliced1x2_ldg8_f2f_tn (grid 152x2x2), i.e. ~120-125 TFLOP/s, only ~39% of the ~312 TFLOP/s dense bf16 ceiling of the same sm80 tensor-op kernels this trace already uses; the o_proj group on the same device demonstrates ~137 TFLOP/s with a better-matched 128x64 stages_64x3 kernel, so cuBLAS heuristic tile choice, not hardware, is the limiter for this exact shape. This group is an existing eligible leaf, phase-pure (all 72 calls prefill), signature-pure (one distinct arg shape), and self-contained: its outputs feed the unchanged SiLU/mul/down_proj path, no reordering or cross-group dependency is needed, and the M=1 decode linear groups are separate groups with separate signatures, so a shape-specialized replacement dispatched only for these 72 calls is a coherent editable boundary with the whole workload still executed unchanged.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the cuBLAS-heuristic 64x128 sliced1x2 GEMM used by the 72 gate/up prefill calls with a kernel tuned for exactly M=256, N=9728, K=2560 bf16 TN (cublasLt algorithm search or a CUTLASS sm80 config with better tile/stage/split-k choice, accumulating in fp32) raises throughput from ~122 toward the 180-220 TFLOP/s already achievable for this size class, cutting per-call time from ~105 us to roughly 58-71 us and the group total from 7.66 ms to ~4.2-5.1 ms. Because these calls sit entirely inside the ttft boundary and are ~36% of prefill CUDA time, the projected clean ttft_ms drops by roughly 2.5-3.4 ms from the 24.12 ms original baseline (about 10-14%), while logits stay within the 0.02 atol/rtol tolerance and greedy tokens remain exact since only GEMM kernel selection changes, not math or dataflow. This is a hypothesis to be tested: diagnostic CUDA deltas must be confirmed against clean paired ttft_ms repeats, and if the tuned kernel does not beat the heuristic under clean timing the selection gains nothing.

proposal.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose boundary is the prefill forward plus argmax and the explicit first-token synchronize. The selected leaf group 0c566a3a363f294c6750 is the 72 prefill gate_proj/up_proj aten::linear.default sites (one per projection per layer, all 36 layers), each exactly one M=256, N=9728, K=2560 bf16 TN GEMM on contiguous operands. Diagnostic evidence in target-resources.json shows cuBLAS dispatches ampere_bf16_s1688gemm_bf16_64x128_sliced1x2_ldg8_f2f_tn (grid 152x2x2, 230 regs/thread, 32KB smem) at 103.7-109.5 us per call, ~7.66 ms total (~36% of the 21.5 ms prefill CUDA time), only ~120-125 TFLOP/s of the ~312 TFLOP/s ceiling of the same sm80 tensor cores; the z=2 grid indicates a split-K style decomposition whose 152-CTA, 1.4-wave tile quantization and per-call split reduction waste throughput at this exact shape. The replacement is one Triton blocked GEMM per site consuming A[256,2560] and B[9728,2560] in their native row-major layouts (no packing, no precompute, no cross-call state), accumulating in fp32 with no split-K; tile/warp/stage configuration is frozen at build from context['parameters'] and tuned by the existing TaskSearch/TPE loop over the declared parameter_space. The hypothesis (to be confirmed by clean paired ttft_ms repeats, not by the diagnostic deltas) is that a shape-matched tile choice moving from 1.4 waves to 2-3 full waves reaches the ~180-220 TFLOP/s class for this size, i.e. ~55-75 us per call and ~4.0-5.4 ms group time, cutting ttft_ms by roughly 2.2-3.4 ms from the 24.12 ms baseline (~9-14%). Every replacement guards the observed signature exactly - shape (1,256,2560)x(9728,2560), strides (655360,2560,1)x(2560,1), bf16, CUDA device matching the current device, bias=None, and grad-mode disabled - and otherwise calls the parent aten::linear, so the decode-phase M=1 linears (separate call ids) and any other invocation are bit-identical to baseline. Because the work per site still executes on every invocation (a real GEMM of the same operands), no fixture-dependent outputs are cached and no calls are eliminated; state lifecycle is unchanged (request-local KV cache created per run by the adapter, weights read-only), no extra synchronization is introduced (single stream, the source's own ttft synchronize remains the boundary), and there are no collectives (single rank; build returns only the rank-local mapping for these 72 rank-0 ids). inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist for this attempt, so no prior worker feedback is incorporated. Launch registers/shared memory in the inventory are treated as configuration observations only, not as measured occupancy or causal effects; no unmeasured transport or memory capability is claimed.

setup_work.persistent_allocations: None. Weights are consumed in place in their native [N,K] row-major (TN) layout; no transposition, packing or replication is performed at build time, so no additional GPU memory is retained and framework.peak_allocated_bytes / lifecycle peaks are expected to match the baseline allocation profile.
setup_work.transient_allocations: Per candidate call one output tensor of 256*9728*2 = 4,985,920 bytes, the same shape and lifetime as the parent aten::linear output allocation; freed through the caching allocator exactly as in the baseline.
setup_work.first_invocation: Triton JIT-compiles the kernel once per process on the first candidate invocation (inside the untimed warmup/quality passes, before the timed repeats); compilation is CPU-side and does not allocate GPU memory beyond the module image. Steady-state calls perform one cached kernel launch each.
setup_work.build_time_work: build(context) only validates the tunable tile configuration (divisibility of 256/9728/2560 by the chosen blocks and an sm80 shared-memory bound of 155648 bytes) and constructs one guarded closure per selected call id; an illegal configuration yields an empty mapping (project unchanged) rather than an error.
setup_work.no_cuda_graphs: No CUDA Graphs are captured and no streams are created; all launches go to the worker's current stream.
setup_work.parameters: Read from context['parameters']; defaults BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=64, GROUP_M=4, num_warps=4, num_stages=4 when the coordinator supplies none.

quality_risks: Numeric: the Triton kernel accumulates the full K=2560 reduction in fp32 registers with a single accumulator per output tile, while the baseline cuBLAS split-K path may combine partial sums in bf16 (torch default allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction=True); the replacement's rounding differs from cuBLAS but is at least as precise as an fp32-accumulated reference. Logits are checked at atol=rtol=0.02 and last-position logit magnitudes make the expected max_abs_error far smaller than the tolerance, but this is verified by the framework's quality run, not asserted here.

Greedy tokens: require_exact_greedy_tokens=true means any argmax near-tie that flips under a different-but-in-tolerance GEMM rounding would fail quality. This risk is intrinsic to changing GEMM kernel selection (the selection's hypothesis accepts it); typical token distributions have logit gaps well above the perturbation scale.

Guard fallback: any invocation whose signature deviates from the observed one (bias present, other shapes/strides/dtypes, non-current device, grad enabled) calls the parent aten::linear unchanged, so semantics are preserved for decode M=1 linears and any unforeseen call pattern; those calls simply get no speedup.
Environment: if Triton or its compiler toolchain is unavailable on the worker, build returns an empty mapping and the project runs unchanged (no improvement, no failure).

Coverage: all 72 selected call sites execute a real GEMM each invocation, so the framework's counted candidate calls and the recaptured plan match the baseline call structure one-to-one; no inner calls are eliminated.

params.name: BLOCK_M
params.description: Rows of the output tile. 128 gives 2 M-blocks (152 CTAs, 2 waves at 128x128); 64 gives 4 M-blocks (304 CTAs, ~3 waves, better SM coverage for M=256).

params.name: BLOCK_N
params.description: Columns of the output tile; N=9728 divides both choices exactly (76 or 38 column blocks).

params.name: BLOCK_K
params.description: Depth of each K=2560 reduction step; all choices divide 2560 exactly, enabling mask-free inner loops.

params.name: GROUP_M
params.description: CTA grouping for L2 reuse of the 49.8 MB B panel across the 2-4 M-blocks.

params.name: num_warps
params.description: Warps per CTA for the tl.dot tile.

params.name: num_stages
params.description: Software pipelining stages; bounded by the shared-memory constraint.

constraints.rationale: The frozen M=256 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.
The frozen N=9728 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.
The frozen K=2560 must tile exactly so the mask-free kernel is valid.

Per-CTA shared memory for both bf16 operand tiles across all pipeline stages must stay inside the sm80 dynamic limit of 166912 bytes with epilogue margin; illegal configurations are rejected by build() as well.
The launch grid must supply at least one CTA per SM (108 SMs on sm80) so the kernel does not under-occupy the device; this prunes e.g. 128x256 (76 CTAs).
